BaseboardId.description:
A representation of a Baseboard ID as used in the inventory subsystem.

This type is essentially the same as a `Baseboard` except it doesn't have a revision or HW type (Gimlet, PC, Unknown).

serial_number.description: Serial number (unique for a given part number)

EccR.description: The first half of a 256 bit elliptic-curve signature: the scalar `r` of an ECDSA pair, or the encoded point `R` of an Ed25519 signature. It is carried as an opaque 256 bit value to which only the signature algorithm assigns meaning.

EccS.description: The second half of a 256 bit elliptic-curve signature: the scalar `s` of an ECDSA pair, or the little-endian scalar `S` of an Ed25519 signature. It is carried as an opaque 256 bit value like [`EccR`].

EncodedSignature.description:
Code phrase encoded signature.

The decoded phrases `r` and `s` together comprise a signature _(r, s)_ over a 256 bit elliptic curve.

The `flags` and `counter` parameters are for the [`SK-*` family of SSH public keys](https://cvsweb.openbsd.org/src/usr.bin/ssh/PROTOCOL.u2f?annotate=HEAD). They should be set to 0 for other key types.

JobId.description: A globally unique identifier for a job within a session.

JobMode.description: How a job runs. The streaming modes allow **unrecorded** I/O.

JobOutputHash.description: SHA3-256 hash of job output, used as a checksum.

JobOutputStream.description: Either the standard output or standard error of a job.

JobStartRequest.description: A request to run the given `command` as `job_id`.

target.description: The sleds this job runs on.

actor.description: The key that requested the cancellation.
The key that submitted the job.

KeyId.description: SHA-256 of a certificate subject or an identity public key, encoded as a pseudorandom code phrase for storage & transport.

Nonce.description: A unique random string. Authentication credentials have two of these: one generated by the server, and one by the client. This structure is agnostic to the syntax of the string.

ProcessError.description:
What went wrong running a job's process or interactive session.

We currently squash inner errors into strings to avoid excessive derivation requirements, but may come to regret that decision.

started_by.description: The key that started the session, where known. Client-side trackers leave it `None`. Servers record the verified starter.

SessionId.description: A globally unique identifier for a session.

SessionSignerNonce.description: The component of the hashed Session ID generated by the signer server.

SessionSushNonce.description: The component of the hashed Session ID generated by the Sush server.

Signed_for_JobStartRequest.description: A signed envelope around some data.

SledHealth.description: One sled's gossip link health, as the answering sled sees it. A silent death can lag `Linked` at TCP's pace.

oneOf.description: Attested, holding a live gossip link.
Known by version or cubby, but no live link.
A state from a build newer than this one.

SledVersion.description: One sled's location, build, and health.

commit.description: The git commit, "-dirty" suffixed for an unclean tree.

JobWait.description: Whether and until what state is reached to wait for a job start/stop request.

Access.description: Attach access to a session's interactive jobs. The session starter always has read-write access. Guests have what they were granted. Read-write means co-driving a shell the job signature authorized, so who deserves it is deployment policy. Recorded output is not gated: it is the customer's data, readable by any authenticated key.
